sentences.text: Dennis Walsh (Mr Walsh) is the person being assessed.
Karen Walsh is the daughter of Dennis Walsh and is present during the assessment.
The assessment is a six-month review of the care package.
The care assessor, Priya Nair, is from the adult social care team.
Brightpath Home Care currently provides four visits per day to Mr Walsh: morning, dinner, tea, and bed.
Mr Walsh reports that the carer who does teatime, Shelley, is good and takes her time.
Mr Walsh cannot button his clothes due to hand difficulties.
Mr Walsh does not go up the stairs and sleeps downstairs.
Mr Walsh uses the frame around the house most of the time, when he remembers.
The carers prepare microwave meals for dinner and tea.
Karen brings a proper dinner round on Sundays.
The carers prompt Mr Walsh's diabetes tablets at morning and night.
Mr Walsh wants carer Lee to stop coming to him and wants someone like Shelley to replace him.
Mr Walsh used to go to the bowls club but has not attended since his hip injury.
Mr Walsh expressed interest in attending a Wednesday lunch club at the community centre on Mill Lane with transport.
Mr Walsh reports that carer Lee is always in a rush and has slapped him twice.
Mr Walsh was slapped across the face with an open hand by carer Lee on two occasions: once when he was slow to get off the bed, and once previously a few weeks back.
Mr Walsh reports that carer Lee grabbed his left arm to pull him up from the commode, and this happened 'most mornings when it's him', including a hard grab on Saturday that 'it [h
Karen Walsh discovered bruises on Mr Walsh's left upper arm when she helped him change his top on Sunday.
The bruises were four in a row, like fingermarks, on the inside of the upper arm, purple in colour.
Karen took photos of the bruises on her phone on Sunday.
Mr Walsh told Karen about the abuse by Lee on the night of Sunday, after initially saying he had knocked it.
Mr Walsh stated he did not want a fuss and did not want to lose the carers.
Mr Walsh has not been hurt by anyone in the family or by anyone else at all, only by carer Lee.
Mr Walsh has not told anyone at Brightpath about the abuse by Lee.
The care assessor will raise a safeguarding concern with the council's safeguarding team about carer Lee slapping and grabbing Mr Walsh.
The care assessor will ring the Brightpath manager this afternoon to request that Lee does not come to Mr Walsh while the issue is investigated.
Karen will keep the photos of the bruises and not delete them for the safeguarding team.
The care assessor will arrange for a GP appointment to examine Mr Walsh's left arm by Friday.
Karen will contact the surgery to book the GP appointment tomorrow.
